rubric.why: Identifies a taxon as a unit of biological classification.
rubric.description: A taxon is a unit of biological classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a unit of classification.

rubric.why: States that a taxon is a group of organisms.
rubric.description: A taxon is a group of organisms at any level of classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a group of organisms.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a unit of biological classification.
It is a group of organisms at any level of classification.

items.followUp: State one difference between mitosis and meiosis in the number of daughter cells produced.

rubric.why: Describes mitosis as one division producing genetically identical daughter cells.
rubric.description: Mitosis is one cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the single division and its outcome.

rubric.why: Describes meiosis as two divisions producing four haploid daughter cells.
rubric.description: Meiosis consists of two divisions and produces four haploid daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the two divisions and their outcome.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is one cell division in which one parent cell forms two genetically identical daughter cells.
Meiosis consists of two successive divisions and forms four haploid daughter cells.

items.followUp: Name the enzyme in saliva and state what it digests.

rubric.why: Identifies chewing as a function of the oral cavity.
rubric.description: The oral cavity breaks food into smaller pieces by chewing (mechanical digestion).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for chewing or mechanical digestion.

rubric.why: Identifies the role of saliva or salivary amylase in starting starch digestion.
rubric.description: Saliva mixes with food, and salivary amylase begins starch digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking saliva or salivary amylase with starch digestion.

modelAnswer: The oral cavity receives food and breaks it into smaller pieces by chewing (mechanical digestion).
Saliva mixes with the food, and salivary amylase begins the digestion of starch.
